description: Figure 8 presents three separate pie charts, each illustrating the problem distribution for a different difficulty level—“easy,” “medium,” and “hard”—based on model correctness under “with knowledge” and “without knowledge” settings using a Zero-Shot approach. Each pie chart is divided into four colored segments corresponding to four categories in the legend: teal for “N+K+” (correct with knowledge), gold for “N−K+” (incorrect without knowledge but correct with knowledge), orange for “N−K−” (incorrect both with and without knowledge), and red for “N+K−” (correct without knowledge but incorrect with knowledge). For the “easy” category, the distribution is 55.4% N+K+, 38.3% N−K+, 4.7% N−K−, and 1.6% N+K−. For “medium,” it is 58.8% N+K+, 35.4% N−K+, 4.8% N−K−, and 1.0% N+K−. For “hard,” the distribution is 37.3% N+K+, 37.9% N−K+, 18.1% N−K−, and 6.7% N+K−. The charts visually emphasize that for easy and medium problems, most correct answers occur with knowledge (N+K+), while for hard problems, the proportion of cases where knowledge does not help (N−K−) or even harms performance (N+K−) is significantly higher. The legend is positioned to the right of the charts, and each pie chart is labeled with its difficulty level above it.
